ideas.title: Log the model that really answered each worker run
ideas.problem: workers.run (workers.py ~line 124) writes info['model'] = the model we requested, and cp.record_usage gets the same. Claude Code can answer with another model (2.1.323 added a stderr warning for exactly this). We would never see it: a worker could run on a weaker model, and the usage table would still say Opus.
ideas.proposal: In workers.run, read the keys of out['modelUsage'] (already parsed for webSearchRequests on line 120). Put them in info['models_used']. If none matches the requested alias/model, log a 'model_substituted' event (agent, asked, got) and add the model to the usage row's note. Also keep the first 300 chars of p.stderr when it contains 'model'. Warn only; never fail the run. Not a protected-file change if done in workers.py by the Builder chat (workers.py is protected from Ghassan).
ideas.gain: Cost and quality numbers stay true; Israa/Tarek/Calina results can be explained when a run was on a different model. Measured by: zero silent mismatches in a week, or a visible event when one happens.
ideas.test: 1) Normal: a Vera run on 'opus' logs models_used=[claude-opus-...] and no event. 2) Edge: a run whose modelUsage has two models (main + helper) logs both, no false event. 3) Failure: feed a fake JSON with modelUsage of another model; expect a model_substituted event and the run still succeeds.
ideas.confidence_why: 2.1.323 changelog (A) confirms the substitution can happen; our code gap read directly (A). Weakest link: no evidence yet that it has happened to us.
ideas.risks: modelUsage may include helper models (e.g. small classifier), causing false alarms: match on the main model only and log helpers quietly.
